analysis_trace: Trial NCT06061991 is a randomized controlled trial testing mobile instant messaging-based lifestyle intervention vs control for GDM prevention in high-risk pregnant Chinese women. Primary endpoint: GDM diagnosis at ~28 weeks. Secondary endpoints include gestational weight gain, hypertensive disorders, pharmacological therapy, mode of birth, gestational age, birthweight, LGA, SGA, preterm birth, neonatal hypoglycemia, neonatal death, stillbirth.

Evidence base: Systematic reviews show lifestyle interventions reduce GDM risk by ~20-30% (RR 0.70-0.80). mHealth interventions show modest additional benefit for weight gain but mixed results for GDM prevention. Asian populations have higher GDM baseline risk (~20-30% in high-risk women). Social cognitive theory-based interventions show moderate effect sizes.

Primary endpoint prediction: Based on meta-analyses of lifestyle interventions for GDM prevention, expected relative risk reduction ~20-25%. Control group GDM incidence estimated 25-30% in high-risk Chinese women. Intervention group expected 18-23%. Probability of meeting superiority threshold (>0% effect) high (~75%), but clinical significance depends on magnitude.

Secondary endpoints: Gestational weight gain likely reduced by ~1-2kg (moderate confidence). Hypertensive disorders may show modest reduction (low confidence). Pharmacological therapy use expected reduced proportionally to GDM reduction. Mode of birth, gestational age, birthweight, LGA/SGA, preterm birth expected modestly improved but underpowered. Neonatal outcomes rare events with wide uncertainty.

Key uncertainties: No direct results available for this specific trial. Intervention intensity via messaging vs in-person counseling may reduce effect size. Control group receives brief advice, not pure usual care, potentially attenuating between-group differences. Sample size 944 provides adequate power for primary endpoint.
Safety: Behavioral intervention expected safe. No serious adverse events anticipated.
